div.head: III Atr 12
div.ab: And æt cynges spǽce lecge man VI healfmarc wedd ⁊ æt eorles ⁊ biscopes XII óran wedd ⁊ æt ælcum þegene VI óran wedd.
Et de placito regis ponatur uadium sex dimid. marcis, comitis et episcopi uadium duodecim oris.
And æt cynges spǽce lecge man VI healfmarc wedd ⁊ æt eorles ⁊ biscopes XII óran wedd ⁊ æt ælcum þegene VI óran wedd.
Und bei Anklage durch den König [Staat] hinterlege [Verklagt]er 6 Halbmark Pfand und bei einer durch Graf oder Bischof 12 Ör Pfand und bei [einer durch] irgend einen Thegn 6 Ör Pfand.

And in a suit brought by the king [the state], let [the accused] deposit 6 half-marks as pledge, and in one brought by an earl or bishop 12 ores as pledge, and in [one brought by] any thegn 6 ores as pledge.

And in the case of an action brought by the king, 6 half-marks shall be deposited as security, and in the case of one brought by an earl or a bishop, 12 ores, and of one brought by a thegn, 6 ores as security.
And in a king’s suit one is to put down six half-marks as a pledge, in an earl’s and bishop’s 12 ores as a pledge, and in any thegn’s six ores as a pledge.
div.note: Quadr. omits the last clause (on the thegn).

note.seg: ore T; letzte Zeile überspringt Quadr.
ore T; Quadr. skips the last line
Laut o. 3, 2² ist eine Fiskalklage durch den öffentlichen Beamten gemeint
As above 3, 2², a fiscal suit brought by the public official is meant
Nicht 5½, wie Phillipps Versuch Agsä. Rg. 179 versteht. S. o. 1, 2²
Not 5½, as Phillipps Versuch Agsä. Rg. 179 understands it. See above 1, 2²
Der Graf steht doppelt so hoch wie der Thegn und gleich dem Bischof auch sonst; s. I 615{b. 1}; Gl Stand 21d. y; Eorl 16; Prozessualpfand 5a
The earl ranks twice as high as the thegn, and equal to the bishop, elsewhere too; see I 615{b. 1}; Gl Stand 21d. y; Eorl 16; Prozessualpfand 5a
Vielleicht umfasst hier das Wort den Vollfreien mit, da dieser sonst fehlen würde; s. o. 11¹. Bei einer Klage durch abhängige, bäuerliche Leute brauchte vermutlich Beklagter kein Pfand zu geben

Perhaps the word here includes the fully free man as well, since he would otherwise be missing; see above 11¹. In a suit brought by dependent peasant folk the defendant presumably did not need to give a pledge

As these laws are provincial rather than national it seems probable that the reference is not to actions brought in the king’s court but rather to actions brought by the king’s representative in other courts, cf. Liebermann’s note, iii. p. 160: ‘eine Fiskalklage durch den öffentlichen Beamten.’
